page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Top: printed page number at left and running head at right. Left margin: one marginal note, "Peregrinorum odium." Main text runs down the page. A centred italic verse line and a chapter heading with its title sit inside the text. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: opportunitas, nonnunquam inftantium negotiorum moles reducitur. Non quid alios pati, fed quid ipfum facere dignum fit, & quid rumor hominum admittat, fecum perpendit. plerique, mortales poftrema memine-re; & in hominibus impiis, fceleris eorum obliti, de-pœna differunt, fi ea paulo fævior fuerit. uti facundè in bello Catilinario Salluftii Cæfar. Atqui moderatior caftigatio hominem afperum, vi non adempta, magis irritaffet. Atque ut idem in eadem oratione Cæfar: qui demiffi in obfcuro vitam agunt, fi quid iracundia deliquere, pauci fciunt; fama atque fortuna eorum pares funt: qui magno imperio præditi, in excelfo ætatem agunt, eorum facta cunćti mortales novere. ita in maxima fortuna minima licentia eft. neque ftudere, neque odiffe, fed minimè irafci decet. quæ apud alios iracundia dicitur, ea in imperio fuperbia atque crude-litas appellatur. quæ Cæfaris admonitio tanto plus vi-rium habet, quanto propius ad veritatem accedunt, quæ fenior Micipfa fidenti ætati & Romanorum fa-vori Jugurthæ occinit: in omni certamine, qui opulen-tior eft, etiam fi accipit injuriam, tamen quia plus po-teft facere videtur. S. B. J. Hæc & fimilia Germani-cum ad manfuetudinis recordationem impellere, & ab ultionis cogitatione, abstrahere potuerint. Quan-quam interdum & Publii Mimi verfus cum applaufu auditur; nec theatri modo, fed & vitæ humani ap-plaufu:

p.i: Veterem ferendo injuriam in vitas novam.

main_text.p: Quem non inaniter pronunciatum effe, Germanicus ab Armenia reverfus, nihil jam profutura lamentatio-ne, didicit.
main_text.head: CXXVII. Vicinitas invidiam, peregrinitas odi-um conflare nata eft.
main_text.p: Peregrino-rum odium.Linguæ enim, morum, veftitus diverfitas efficacius animos, quam vicinorum æmulatio, diftrahit. Arme-nii maximis imperiis interjecti, & sapius discordes sunt, adversus Romanos odio, & in Parthum invidia, Quam-vis

page.notes: The scan shows a small stray mark to the right of "eorum" in the first lines; not printed text, so omitted. The left marginal note is printed in two lines ("Peregrino-" / "rum odium."), given here as one note. Italic extent in the last paragraph (from "interjecti" onwards) is uncertain from the scan. "in vitas novam" is transcribed with a space as it appears in print. The chapter number is combined with its title in one heading (level 2) since no division word (CAPUT etc.) is printed.
